editorial.headline: Toll-Road Operations: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This is an operational toll-road and toll-bridge activity with full national foreign-ownership scope, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this toll-road activity as PMA in Bali today, despite a national foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. KBLI 52213 concerns the business of organizing and operating toll roads or toll bridges, including the traffic services through which vehicles use them. That includes running the undertaking itself and serving vehicle traffic in either road or bridge form. Its boundary is deliberately operational: construction and maintenance of a toll road or bridge are outside this activity.

At the national level, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA. The record opens it at the Besar scale only, giving the classification a clear commercial frame without stretching it beyond the evidence. The 100% ceiling means foreign ownership may reach full ownership nationally, under the cited Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. In classification terms, the registrant is the enterprise that organizes and operates the toll-road or toll-bridge business and its vehicle-traffic service; construction or maintenance does not become part of the activity. The scale requirement also matters because Besar is the only scale listed as open.

Bali produces the more consequential reading. For this activity at Besar scale, the OSS risk assessment is Low or Medium-Low across every scope in the record. Bali’s moratorium blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities throughout the province, permanently. The present classification is therefore Blocked (risk class): a foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali. This is expressly island-wide rather than limited to a particular locality, and it is a bar on PMA registration arising from the moratorium referenced to May 2026.

The national and Bali positions are different rather than inconsistent. Nationally, the activity permits up to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, the risk-based provincial rule prevents its PMA registration. The reading begins with the actual scope—operations and vehicle traffic service—and ends with the location-specific outcome. A national opening is not, in this case, a route to PMA registration in Bali.
